rot.borda.demos.espeto.1: Defense demonstration: now let us think for Black. The white king is on f4, on the same file as the queen. Look for the rook check.
rot.borda.demos.espeto.2: Check on f2, along the f-file. The white king stands between the rook and the queen: a skewer.
rot.borda.demos.espeto.3: The white king gets out of check, and the queen on f7 is left undefended on the rook's file.
rot.borda.demos.espeto.4: The rook captures the queen, and now Black is the one winning. Back to White: before moving the king, check whether it lands on the queen's line.
rot.borda.demos.garfo.1: Attack demonstration: Black to move. The rook on b7 is glued to the black king. See what happens if it moves away from it.
rot.borda.demos.garfo.2: The rook goes to f7 and cuts your king off on the f-file, but it is far from the black king, undefended.
rot.borda.demos.garfo.3: Check on g6, along the sixth rank, and the queen attacks f7 along the diagonal: a fork, king and rook at once.
rot.borda.demos.garfo.4: The king gets out of check, and the rook is still undefended. Blocking the check on f6 does not save it either.
rot.borda.demos.garfo.5: Your queen captures the rook, with check. Far from its king and undefended, the rook fell to a fork.
rot.borda.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: the black king and rook are in the center. The rook on c7, glued to the king, is protected by it, and the queen cannot win it with a fork.
rot.borda.ideia.ex1.e2: The plan is to cut off the king: the queen takes ranks, files and diagonals from it, as the h3–c8 diagonal takes e6 and d7, and your king steps up to squeeze, until the black king reaches the edge.
rot.borda.ideia.ex1.l1: Your king steps up to d4 and takes c5, d5 and e5 from the black king. On e3, it would stand on the queen's rank, and the rook would check on c3: a skewer, and the queen would fall.
rot.borda.ideia.ex1.l2: The rook goes to c6, still glued to the king, and cuts your king off on the c-file.
rot.borda.ideia.ex1.l3: Check on a3, along the diagonal to f8. Blocking on c5 would leave the rook pinned; the king leaves d6, and e7 is on the diagonal too.
rot.borda.ideia.ex1.l4: The king falls back to d7, glued to the rook, which stays protected.
rot.borda.ideia.ex1.l5: Your king comes up against the rook and takes d6 and e6 from the black king. The rook is attacked, but the black king protects it.
rot.borda.ideia.ex1.l6: The rook leaves the attack and goes back to c7, next to the king, where it stays protected.
rot.borda.ideia.ex1.l7: Check on a4, along the diagonal to e8; c6, d6 and e6 belong to your king.
rot.borda.ideia.ex1.l8: The king goes to c8, glued to the rook. King on the edge and rook beside it: the second-rank defense, which you already know how to beat.
rot.borda.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: back to the position where your king has just reached d5. Instead of returning to its king, the rook can move away from it, and that is how Black resists longest.
rot.borda.ideia.ex2.l1: The rook goes to f6 and cuts your king off on the sixth rank, but it is far from the black king, undefended.
rot.borda.ideia.ex2.l2: Check on a7, along the seventh rank. c6, d6 and e6 belong to your king, and the black king must go to the eighth rank.
rot.borda.ideia.ex2.l3: The king goes to e8, on the edge. The rook is still far from it, on f6.
rot.borda.ideia.ex2.l4: The queen cuts off the seventh rank, and the black king only has f8. Far from its king, the rook is exposed: every move, check for a check that also attacks it.
rot.borda.pratica.centro.fim: The rook fell. The queen cut off the black king, your king came closer, and the rook found no skewer, no fork and no trade.
rot.borda.pratica.centro.p: Attack: now you play alone. Cut off the black king with the queen, bring your king closer and, every move, check whether the rook gets a skewer or a fork.
rot.borda.pratica.coluna.fim: End of the chapter: from the center to the edge, the queen cut off and your king came closer, until the rook fell.
rot.borda.pratica.coluna.p: Attack: one more, a longer one. Cut off the black king with the queen, bring your king closer and, before each move, check whether the rook gets a skewer, a fork or a trade.
rot.borda.pratica.corte.fim: Your king touched the rook, and the check on c3 took the c-file, b4 and d4 from the black king. On d5, it would move away from the rook, and the check on a5 would win it.
rot.borda.pratica.corte.p: We do it together: two White moves. Bring your king to attack the rook without walking into a fork; the rook runs, and the queen gives the check that cuts off the black king.
rot.borda.pratica.corte.rei.1: This move does not lose, but it does not squeeze either: your king does not attack the rook, and the black king keeps its squares.
rot.borda.pratica.corte.rei.2: Look for the square where your king touches the rook and, at the same time, protects d6, where the rook would give check.
rot.borda.pratica.corte.xeque.1: This move does not lose, but it leaves the black king too many squares.
rot.borda.pratica.corte.xeque.2: Look for the check along the c-file that also takes b4 and d4 from the black king.
rot.borda.pratica.err.afogaTorre.1: The rook checks and attacks the queen: capturing it stalemates the black king, and stepping out of check gives up the queen.
rot.borda.pratica.err.afogaTorre.2: Before moving the king, look at the black king's squares: if it has none, capturing the rook may stalemate it.
rot.borda.pratica.err.espeto.1: The rook checks along the line joining your king to the queen: a skewer. The king gets out of check, and the rook captures the queen.
rot.borda.pratica.err.espeto.2: Do not leave king and queen on the same rank or file if the rook can check from the other side of the king.
rot.borda.pratica.err.espetoTroca.1: Skewer: the rook checks along the line of your king and queen. The king guards the queen, but the rook captures it and your king recaptures: a draw.
rot.borda.pratica.err.espetoTroca.2: Do not leave king and queen on the same line if the rook can check from the other side of the king.
rot.borda.pratica.err.garfoTroca.1: The rook checks and, on the same line, attacks the queen: a fork. To save the queen, you capture the rook, and the black king recaptures: a draw.
rot.borda.pratica.err.garfoTroca.2: Before moving the king, check whether the rook can give a check on a line that also runs through the queen.
rot.borda.pratica.err.recaptura.1: The queen captures the rook, but the black king recaptures: only the two kings are left, and it is a draw.
rot.borda.pratica.err.recaptura.2: Capture the rook only when it is undefended, away from the black king.
rot.borda.pratica.err.solta.1: The queen was left unprotected, within reach of the rook or the black king: it is captured, and now Black is the one winning.
rot.borda.pratica.err.solta.2: Before each move, check that the queen's new square is protected or out of reach of the rook and the black king.
rot.borda.pratica.err.tapa.1: The rook blocks the check, protected by the black king, and pins the queen to your king. The queen can only capture the rook, and the black king recaptures: a draw.
rot.borda.pratica.err.tapa.2: Before giving check, see whether the rook can step in the way, protected by the black king.
rot.borda.pratica.err.troca.1: The rook captures the queen, and your king recaptures: only the two kings are left, and it is a draw.
rot.borda.pratica.err.troca.2: On the rook's line and protected only by the king, the queen can be traded. Put the queen where the rook cannot reach it.
rot.borda.pratica.fins.afogado: Stalemate: a draw. Before a move without check, make sure the black king still has a square.
rot.borda.pratica.fins.insuficiente: Only the kings are left: a draw. Capture the rook only when the black king cannot capture the queen right after.
rot.borda.pratica.fins.limite: The move limit ran out before the rook fell. Cut off the black king with the queen and bring your king closer every move.
rot.borda.pratica.fins.repeticao: The position repeated three times: a draw. Each move should take a square from the black king or bring your king closer.
